name: com.whoreadsthe/agents
title: Who reads the web
description: Check whether a web request really comes from the AI agent it claims to be. Read agent records.

tools.name: identify_request
tools.description: Check whether a web request really comes from the AI agent or crawler its user agent names. Give the request's User-Agent header and its IP address. Returns the claimed agent and the strongest check passed: the vendor's published IP list, reverse DNS, or a network block registered to the vendor. It cannot check request signatures. What you send is used for the check and is not stored.

ip.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address the request came from.

tools.name: check_requests
tools.description: Check up to 50 web requests at once, for example the unique user agent and address pairs from an access log, and learn for each whether it really comes from the AI agent or crawler its user agent names. Same checks as identify_request; results come back in the order sent, by index. Remove duplicates before sending. Send no paths: to check robots.txt, apply its rules yourself. To check a whole log without sending it, download https://whoreadsthe.com/check/data.json and follow the rules at https://whoreadsthe.com/api#local. What you send is used for the check and is not stored.

requests.description: The requests to check: each a User-Agent header value and the IPv4 or IPv6 address it came from.

tools.name: agent_profile
tools.description: Get the record of one AI agent or crawler: what its vendor documents (user agent, IP list, robots.txt policy), what this site has observed of it, and where the two disagree. Use list_agents to find the agent id.

agent_id.description: The agent id from list_agents, for example "gptbot" or "claude-user".

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List every AI agent and crawler in the registry, with its id, vendor, purpose and a short summary of what this site has observed.

tools.name: start_test_run
tools.description: Start a run of this site's test course for AI agents. Returns a private set of test addresses and a result address. Fetching the test pages records what the visitor did: robots.txt, a blocked page, a redirect into a blocked path, JavaScript, Markdown, a re-check, signatures, backing off when asked to wait, links marked nofollow, a link that ends a sentence, and an endless series of pages. The run is open for 24 hours. Anyone with the result address can read the result.

tools.name: test_run_result
tools.description: Read the result of a test course run: for each visitor, how it identified itself and what it did on each test. Facts only, no score.

run_id.description: The run code returned by start_test_run.

tools.name: submit_declaration
tools.description: Ask this site to read and check the declaration file a domain publishes at https://<domain>/.well-known/whoreadsthe.json, which declares the AI agents or crawlers the domain operates. Accepted agents get a record on this site. The file format is described at https://whoreadsthe.com/declare. At most 5 calls a minute per address.

domain.description: The registrable domain that publishes the declaration file, such as example.com.

tools.name: decide_robots_txt
tools.description: For a site owner: turn yes or no answers about AI agents into the robots.txt lines that put them into effect. Answer by purpose (training, search, user, agentic) and, where wanted, for single agents by id. The result has the lines to add to robots.txt and, for every agent in the registry, its robots.txt name, what its vendor states about following robots.txt and what this site has observed. A "no" disallows the agent; a "yes" adds no line. Crawlers that also build ordinary web search (Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot) are never changed by a question, only one by one. Nothing that is chosen is stored.

training.description: May AI vendors use the pages to train models?

search.description: May AI search list and quote the pages?

user.description: May an assistant fetch a page when a person asks about it?

agentic.description: May an agent browse and act on the site for a person?

agents.description: Answers for single agents, by the id from list_agents, for example {"googlebot": "no"}. They win over the answers by purpose.
